newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI Fortuna 1996 net at PLN 38.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI Fortuna 1996 net at PLN 38.7 mln.

text.p: National Investment Fund Fortuna (NFI No. 13) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme made a net profit of 38.7 million zlotys last year after losing 7.8 million zlotys in 1995, the fund said in an issue prospectus.
The fund said it planned to float five of its firms in 1997 and 1998 and that strategic investors were sought for more than a dozen others through capital rises or outright share sales.

Fortuna said that among its largest companies, strategic investors were sought for chemicals and plastics firm Elana SA and metals and engineering firms Fazos SA and Andoria SA, though Elana might be floated instead.
It said garment maker Wistil SA is to be listed on the Warsaw bourse in this year's fourth quarter.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
Each NFI has 31,026,185 shares. The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
